name: la.1
text: Adoro te devote, latens Deitas,

name: la.1
text: Quae sub his figuris vere latitas:

name: la.1
text: Tibi se cor meum totum subiicit,

name: la.1
text: Quia te contemplans totum deficit.

name: en.singable
text:
Godhead here in hiding, whom I do adore,
Masked by these bare shadows, shape and nothing more,
See, Lord, at thy service low lies here a heart
Lost, all lost in wonder at the God thou art.

name: la.1
text: Visus, tactus, gustus in te fallitur,

name: la.1
text: Sed auditu solo tuto creditur.

name: la.1
text: Credo quidquid dixit Dei Filius:

name: la.1
text: Nil hoc verbo Veritatis verius.

name: en.singable
la.1
text: In cruce latebat sola Deitas,

name: la.1
text: At hic latet simul et humanitas;

name: la.1
text:
Ambo tamen credens atque confitens,
Peto quod petivit latro paenitens.

name: en.singable
text:
On the cross thy godhead made no sign to men,
Here thy very manhood steals from human ken:
Both are my confession, both are my belief,
And I pray the prayer of the dying thief.

name: la.1
text: Plagas, sicut Thomas, non intueor;

name: la.1
text: Deum tamen meum te confiteor.

name: la.1
text:
Fac me tibi semper magis credere,
In te spem habere, te diligere.

name: en.singable
text:
I am not like Thomas, wounds I cannot see,
But can plainly call thee Lord and God as he;
Let me to a deeper faith daily nearer move,
Daily make me harder hope and dearer love.

name: la.1
text: O memoriale mortis Domini!

name: la.1
text: Panis vivus, vitam praestans homini!

name: la.1
text:
Praesta meae menti de te vivere,
Et te illi semper dulce sapere.

name: en.singable
text:
O thou our reminder of Christ crucified,
Living Bread, the life of us for whom he died,
Lend this life to me then: feed and feast my mind,
There be thou the sweetness man was meant to find.

name: la.1
text: Pie pellicane, Iesu Domine,

name: la.1
text: Me immundum munda tuo sanguine:

name: la.1
text:
Cuius una stilla salvum facere
Totum mundum quit ab omni scelere.

name: en.singable
text:
Bring the tender tale true of the Pelican;
Bathe me, Jesu Lord, in what thy bosom ran—
Blood whereof a single drop has power to win
All the world forgiveness of its world of sin.

name: la.1
text: Iesu, quem velatum nunc aspicio,

name: la.1
text: Oro fiat illud quod tam sitio;

name: la.1
text:
Ut te revelata cernens facie,
Visu sim beatus tuae gloriae. Amen.

name: en.singable
text:
Jesu, whom I look at shrouded here below,
I beseech thee send me what I thirst for so,
Some day to gaze on thee face to face in light
And be blest for ever with thy glory's sight. Amen.

name: la.1
text:
Pange, lingua, gloriosi
Corporis mysterium,
Sanguinisque pretiosi,

name: en.elegant
text: Sing, my tongue, the mystery of the glorious Body and of the precious Blood

name: la.1
text:
Quem in mundi pretium
Fructus ventris generosi
Rex effudit gentium.

name: en.elegant
text: which the King of the nations, fruit of a noble womb, poured out as the price of the world.

name: en.singable
text:
Sing, my tongue, the Saviour's glory,
Of His Flesh the mystery sing;
Of the Blood, all price exceeding,
Shed by our immortal King,
Destined, for the world's redemption,
From a noble womb to spring.

name: en.literal
text: Sing, O my tongue, the mystery of the glorious Body and of the precious Blood, which the King of the Gentiles, the fruit of a noble womb, shed for the redemption of the world.

name: la.1
text:
Nobis datus, nobis natus
Ex intacta Virgine,
Et in mundo conversatus,
Sparso verbi semine,
Sui moras incolatus
Miro clausit ordine.

name: en.elegant
text: Given to us, born to us of a Virgin untouched, and having dwelt in the world, having scattered the seed of the word, he closed the days of his sojourn in wondrous order.

name: en.singable
text:
Of a pure and spotless Virgin
Born for us on earth below,
He, as Man, with man conversing,
Stayed, the seeds of truth to sow;
Then He closed in solemn order
Wondrously His life of woe.

name: en.literal
text: Given to us, and born for us of a stainless Virgin, He dwelt on earth sowing the seed of the word, and closed in a wondrous manner the days of His earthly sojourning.

name: la.1
text:
In supremae nocte cenae
Recumbens cum fratribus,
Observata lege plene
Cibis in legalibus,
Cibum turbae duodenae
Se dat suis manibus.

name: en.elegant
text: On the night of the last supper, reclining with his brethren, the law having been fully observed in the foods it prescribed, he gives himself with his own hands as food to the company of twelve.

name: en.singable
text:
On the night of that Last Supper
Seated with His chosen band,
He, the Paschal victim eating,
First fulfills the Law's command:
Then as Food to all His brethren
Gives Himself with His own hand.

name: en.literal
text: On the night of the Last Supper, reclining with His brethren -- the Law having been fully complied with in regard to legal meats -- with His own hands, He gives Himself as Food to the assembled twelve.

name: la.1
text:
Verbum caro, panem verum
Verbo carnem efficit:

name: en.elegant
text: The Word made flesh makes true bread flesh by a word,

name: la.1
text: Fitque sanguis Christi merum,

name: en.elegant
text: and the wine becomes the blood of Christ;

name: la.1
text:
Et si sensus deficit,
Ad firmandum cor sincerum
Sola fides sufficit.

name: en.elegant
text: and if sense fails, faith alone suffices to strengthen a sincere heart.

name: en.singable
text:
Word made Flesh, the bread of nature
By His word to Flesh He turns;
Wine into His Blood He changes:
What though sense no change discerns?
Only be the heart in earnest,
Faith her lesson quickly learns.

name: en.literal
text: The Word-made-Flesh changes by His word true bread into His Flesh; and wine becomes the Blood of Christ; and if the intellect does not grasp this, faith alone suffices to make sure the sincere heart.

name: la.1
text:
Tantum ergo Sacramentum
Veneremur cernui:

name: en.elegant
text: So great a Sacrament, therefore, let us venerate with bowed heads;

name: la.1
text:
Et antiquum documentum
Novo cedat ritui:

name: en.elegant
text: and let the old pattern yield to the new rite;

name: la.1
text:
Praestet fides supplementum
Sensuum defectui.

name: en.elegant
text: let faith supply what the senses fail to give.

name: en.singable
en.literal
text: Let us therefore, prostrate, adore so great a Sacrament, and let the Old Law give way to the New Ordinance; let faith supplement the weakness of the senses.

name: la.1
text:
Genitori, Genitoque
Laus et iubilatio,
Salus, honor, virtus quoque
Sit et benedictio:

name: en.elegant
text: To the Begetter and the Begotten be praise and jubilation, salvation, honor, might, and blessing also;

name: la.1
text:
Procedenti ab utroque
Compar sit laudatio. Amen.

name: en.elegant
text: to the One proceeding from both be equal praise. Amen.

name: en.singable
text:
To the everlasting Father,
And the Son who reigns on high,
With the Holy Ghost proceeding
Forth from Each eternally,
Be salvation, honor, blessing,
Might, and endless majesty.

name: en.literal
text: To the Father and to the Son be praise, glory, salvation, honor, power, and benediction also! and to Him proceeding from Them both be equal praise.

name: la.1
text: Lauda Sion Salvatorem,

name: la.1
text:
Lauda ducem et pastorem,
In hymnis et canticis.

name: la.1
text: Quantum potes, tantum aude:

name: la.1
text:
Quia major omni laude,
Nec laudare sufficis.

name: en.singable
text:
Praise, O Sion, praise thy Saviour,
Shepherd, Prince, with glad behavior,
Praise in hymn and canticle:
Sing His glory without measure,
For the merit of your Treasure
Never shall your praises fill.

name: en.literal
text: Praise, O Sion, thy Saviour, praise thy Leader and thy Shepherd in hymns and canticles. As much as thou canst, so much darest thou, for He is above all praise, nor art thou able to praise Him enough.

name: la.1
text:
Laudis thema specialis,
Panis vivus et vitalis
Hodie proponitur.

name: la.1
text:
Quem in sacræ mensa cœnæ
Turbæ fratrum duodenæ
Datum non ambigitur.

name: en.singable
text:
Wondrous theme of mortal singing,
Living Bread and Bread life-bringing,
Sing we on this joyful day:
At the Lord's own table given
To the twelve as Bread from Heaven,
Doubting not we firmly say.

name: en.literal
text: To-day there is given us a special theme of praise, the Bread both living and life-giving, which, it is not to be doubted, was given to the assembly of the brethren, twelve in number, at the table of the holy Supper.

name: la.1
text: Sit laus plena, sit sonora,

name: la.1
text:
Sit jucunda, sit decora,
Mentis jubilatio.

name: la.1
text: Dies enim solemnis agitur,

name: la.1
text:
In qua mensæ prima recolitur
Hujus institutio.

name: en.singable
text:
Sing His praise with voice sonorous;
Every heart shall hear the chorus
Swell in melody sublime:
For this day the Shepherd gave us
Flesh and Blood to feed and save us,
Lasting to the end of time.

name: en.literal
text: Let our praise be full and sounding; let the jubilations of the soul be joyous and becoming; for that solemn day is now being celebrated, on which is commemorated the first institution of this table.

name: la.1
text:
In hac mensa novi Regis,
Novum Pascha novæ legis,
Phase vetus terminat.

name: la.1
text:
Vetustatem novitas,
Umbram fugat veritas,

name: la.1
text: Noctem lux eliminat.

name: en.singable
text:
At the new King's sacred table,
The new Law's new Pasch is able
To succeed the ancient Rite:
Old to new its place hath given,
Truth has far the shadows driven,
Darkness flees before the Light.

name: en.literal
text: At this table of the new King, the new Pasch of the New Law puts an end to the ancient Pasch. The new supplants the old, truth puts to flight the shadow, day banishes night.

name: la.1
text: Quod in cœna Christus gessit,

name: la.1
text:
Faciendum hoc expressit
In sui memoriam.

name: la.1
text:
Docti sacris institutis,
Panem, vinum in salutis
Consecramus hostiam.

name: en.singable
text:
And as He hath done and planned it--
"Do this"--hear His love command it,
"For a memory of me."
Learnèd, Lord, in Thy own science,
Bread and wine, in sweet compliance,
As a Host we offer Thee.

name: en.literal
text: What Christ did at that Supper, the same He commanded to be done in remembrance of Him. Taught by His sacred precepts, we consecrate bread and wine into the Victim of salvation.

name: la.1
text: Dogma datur Christianis,

name: la.1
text:
Quod in carnem transit panis,
Et vinum in sanguinem.

name: la.1
text: Quod non capis, quod non vides,

name: la.1
text:
Animosa firmat fides,
Præter rerum ordinem.

name: en.singable
text:
Thus in faith the Christian heareth:
That Christ's Flesh as bread appeareth,
And as wine His Precious Blood:
Though we feel it not nor see it,
Living Faith that doth decree it
All defects of sense makes good.

name: en.literal
text: This is the dogma given to Christians, that bread is changed into Flesh and wine into Blood. What thou dost not understand, what thou dost not see, a lively faith confirms in a supernatural manner.

name: la.1
text:
Sub diversis speciebus,
Signis tantum, et non rebus,
Latent res eximiæ.

name: la.1
text: Caro cibus, sanguis potus:

name: la.1
text:
Manet tamen Christus totus,
Sub utraque specie.

name: en.singable
text:
Lo! beneath the species dual
(Signs not things), is hid a jewel
Far beyond creation's reach!
Though His Flesh as food abideth,
And His Blood as drink--He hideth
Undivided under each.

name: en.literal
text: Under different species (different) in externals (signis) only, and not in reality (rebus), wondrous substances lie hidden. Flesh is food, Blood is drink: nevertheless Christ remains entire under each species.

name: la.1
text:
A sumente non concisus,
Non confractus, non divisus:
Integer accipitur.

name: la.1
text:
Sumit unus, sumunt mille:
Quantum isti, tantum ille:

name: la.1
text: Nec sumptus consumitur.

name: en.singable
text:
Whoso eateth It can never
Break the Body, rend or sever;
Christ entire our hearts doth fill:
Thousands eat the Bread of Heaven,
Yet as much to one is given:
Christ, though eaten, bideth still.

name: en.literal
text: By the recipient the whole (Christ) is received; He is neither cut, broken, nor divided. One receives Him; a thousand receive Him: as much as the thousand receive, so much does the one receive; though eaten He is not diminished.

name: la.1
text:
Sumunt boni, sumunt mali:
Sorte tamen inæquali,
Vitæ, vel interitus.

name: la.1
text: Mors est malis, vita bonis:

name: la.1
text:
Vide paris sumptionis,
Quam sit dispar exitus.

name: en.singable
en.literal
text: The good receive Him, the bad receive Him, but with what unequal consequences of life or death. It is death to the unworthy, life to the worthy: behold then of a like reception, how unlike may be the result!

name: la.1
text:
Fracto demum Sacramento
Ne vacilles, sed memento,
Tantum esse sub fragmento,

name: la.1
text: Quantum toto tegitur.

name: la.1
text: Nulla rei fit scissura:

name: la.1
text: Signi tantum fit fractura:

name: la.1
text:
Qua nec status, nec statura
Signati minuitur.

name: en.singable
text:
When at last the Bread is broken,
Doubt not what the Lord hath spoken:
In each part the same love-token,
The same Christ, our hearts adore:
For no power the Thing divideth--
'Tis the symbols He provideth,
While the Saviour still abideth
Undiminished as before.

name: en.literal
text: When the Sacrament is broken, doubt not, but remember, that there is just as much hidden in a fragment, as there is in the whole. There is no division of the substance, only a breaking of the species takes place, by which neither the state nor stature of the substance signified is diminished.

name: la.1
text:
Ecce panis angelorum,
Factus cibus viatorum:

name: la.1
text:
Vere panis filiorum,
Non mittendus canibus.

name: la.1
text: In figuris præsignatur,

name: la.1
text: Cum Isaac immolatur:

name: la.1
text: Agnus Paschæ deputatur:

name: la.1
text: Datur manna patribus.

name: en.singable
text:
Hail, angelic Bread of Heaven,
Now the pilgrim's hoping-leaven,
Yea, the Bread to children given
That to dogs must not be thrown:
In the figures contemplated,
'Twas with Isaac immolated,
By the Lamb 'twas antedated,
In the Manna it was known.

name: en.literal
text: Lo, the Bread of Angels is made the food of earthly pilgrims: truly it is the Bread of children, let it not be cast to dogs. It was prefigured in types,--when Isaac was immolated, when the Paschal Lamb was sacrificed, when Manna was given to the fathers.

name: la.1
text: Bone Pastor, panis vere,

name: la.1
text: Jesu, nostri miserere:

name: la.1
text: Tu nos pasce, nos tuere:

name: la.1
text:
Tu nos bona fac videre
In terra viventium.

name: la.1
text:
Tu qui cuncta scis et vales:
Qui nos pascis hic mortales:
Tuos ibi commensales,
Cohæredes et sodales
Fac sanctorum civium.

name: en.singable
text:
O Good Shepherd, still confessing
Love, in spite of our transgressing,--
Here Thy blessèd Food possessing,
Make us share Thine every blessing
In the land of life and love:
Thou, whose power hath all completed
And Thy Flesh as Food hath meted,
Make us, at Thy table seated,
By Thy Saints, as friends be greeted,
In Thy paradise above.

name: en.literal
text: O Good Shepherd, True Bread, O Jesus, have mercy on us: feed us and protect us: make us see good things in the land of the living. Thou who knowest all things and canst do all things, who here feedest us mortals, make us there be Thy guests, the co-heirs, and companions of the heavenly citizens.

name: la.1
text: Sacris solemniis juncta sint gaudia,

name: la.1
text: Et ex præcordiis sonent præconia;

name: la.1
text:
Recedant vetera, nova sint omnia,
Corda, voces, et opera.

name: en.singable
text:
At this our solemn Feast,
Let holy joys abound,
And from the inmost breast
Let songs of praise resound;
Let ancient rites depart,
And all be new around,
In ev'ry act and voice and heart.

name: en.literal
text: With this sacred solemnity let our joys be blended, and from our inmost heart let praises resound; let old things depart, let all be new--hearts, words, and works.

name: la.1
text: Noctis recolitur cœna novissima,

name: la.1
text:
Qua Christus creditur agnum et azyma
Dedisse fratribus, juxta legitima
Priscis indulta patribus.

name: en.singable
text:
Remember we that eve,
When, the Last Supper spread,
Christ, as we all believe,
The lamb, with leavenless bread,
Among His brethren shared,
And thus the Law obeyed,
Of old unto their sires declared.

name: en.literal
text: Of that night, the Last Supper is recalled to mind, at which we believe that Christ gave the lamb and the leavenless bread to His brethren, according to the legal precepts given to the ancient fathers.

name: la.1
text:
Post agnum typicum, expletis epulis,
Corpus Dominicum datum discipulis,
Sic totum omnibus, quod totum singulis,
Ejus fatemur manibus.

name: en.singable
text:
The typic lamb consumed,
The legal Feast complete,
The Lord unto the Twelve
His Body gave to eat;
The whole to all, no less
The whole to each, did mete
With His own hands, as we confess.

name: en.literal
text: After the typic lamb, and when the meal was ended, we profess that Our Lord, with His own hands, gave His Body to His brethren; He so gave It that the whole was given to all, and the whole to each.

name: la.1
text: Dedit fragilibus corporis ferculum,

name: la.1
text:
Dedit et tristibus sanguinis poculum,
Dicens: accipite quod trado vasculum,

name: la.1
text: Omnes ex eo bibite.

name: en.singable
text:
He gave them, weak and frail,
His Flesh, their food to be;
On them, downcast and sad,
His Blood bestowèd He:
And thus to them He spake,
"Receive this Cup from Me,
And all of you of this partake."

name: en.literal
text: He gave to the weak His Body as food, and He gave to the sad the cup of His Blood, saying: Receive ye the cup which I give to you, drink ye all of it.

name: la.1
text: Sic sacrificium istud instituit,

name: la.1
text:
Cujus officium committi voluit
Solis presbyteris, quibus sic congruit,
Ut sumant, et dent ceteris.

name: en.singable
text:
So He this Sacrifice
To institute did will,
And charged His priests alone
That office to fulfil:
In them He did confide:
To whom pertaineth still
To take, and to the rest divide.

name: en.literal
text: Thus He instituted this Sacrifice (Sacrament) the administration of which He willed should be entrusted to priests alone, whom it thus behooves to receive it themselves, and to give it to others.

name: la.1
text: Panis angelicus fit panis hominum;

name: la.1
text: Dat panis cœlicus figuris terminum:

name: la.1
text:
O res mirabilis, manducat Dominum
Pauper, servus, et humilis.

name: en.singable
text:
Thus Angels' Bread is made
The Bread of man to-day:
The Living Bread from Heaven
With figures doth away:
O wondrous gift indeed!
The poor and lowly may
Upon their Lord and Master feed.

name: en.literal
text: The Bread of Angels becomes the Bread of men; the Bread of Heaven puts an end to types; O wondrous thing, the poor, the servant, and the lowly, eat their Lord!

name: la.1
text: Te trina Deitas unaque poscimus,

name: la.1
text: Sic nos tu visita, sicut te colimus:

name: la.1
text:
Per tuas semitas duc nos quo tendimus,
Ad lucem, quam inhabitas.

name: en.singable
text:
O Triune Deity,
To Thee we meekly pray,
So mayst Thou visit us,
As we our homage pay;
And in Thy footsteps bright
Conduct us on our way
To where Thou dwell'st in cloudless light.

name: en.literal
text: O triune Deity, we beseech Thee, that Thou visit us, as we adore Thee; lead us by Thy ways, whither we direct our steps, to the light wherein Thou dost dwell.

name: la.1
text:
Verbum supernum prodiens,
Nec Patris linquens dexteram,
Ad opus suum exiens,
Venit ad vitæ vesperam.

name: en.singable
text:
The Heav'nly Word proceeding forth,
Yet leaving not the Father's side,
And going to His work on earth
Had reached at length life's eventide.

name: en.literal
text: The Heavenly Word going forth, yet not leaving the right hand of His Father, went forth to His allotted work, and arrived at the evening of His life.

name: la.1
text:
In mortem a discipulo
Suis tradendus æmulis,
Prius in vitæ ferculo
Se tradidit discipulis.

name: en.singable
text:
By false disciple to be given
To foemen for His Blood athirst,
Himself, the Living Bread from Heaven,
He gave to His disciples first.

name: en.literal
text: When about to be delivered over to His enemies, by a disciple, to be put to death, He first gave Himself to His disciples as the Bread of Life.

name: la.1
text:
Quibus sub bina specie
Carnem dedit et sanguinem;

name: la.1
text:
Ut duplicis substantiæ
Totum cibaret hominem.

name: en.singable
text:
To them He gave, in two-fold kind,
His very Flesh, His very Blood:
In love's own fulness thus designed
Of the whole man to be the food.

name: en.literal
text: To them He gave His Flesh and His Blood under a twofold species, that He might wholly feed man, who is of a twofold nature.

name: la.1
text:
Se nascens dedit socium,
Convescens in edulium,
Se moriens in pretium,

name: la.1
text: Se regnans dat in præmium.

name: en.singable
en.literal
text: By being born, He gave Himself to us as our companion; at the table, He gave Himself as our food; dying He gave Himself as our ransom; now reigning in glory He gives Himself as our reward.

name: la.1
text: O salutaris hostia,

name: la.1
text: Quæ cœli pandis ostium,

name: la.1
text: Bella premunt hostilia,

name: la.1
text: Da robur, fer auxilium.

name: en.singable
text:
O saving Victim, opening wide
The gate of heaven to man below,
Our foes press on from every side,
Thine aid supply, Thy strength bestow.

name: en.literal
text: O Saving Victim, that openest the gate of heaven; hostile attacks oppress us, give us strength, bring us aid.

name: la.1
text:
Uni trinoque Domino,
Sit sempiterna gloria:

name: la.1
text:
Qui vitam sine termino
Nobis donet in patria.

name: en.singable
text:
To Thy great Name be endless praise,
Immortal Godhead, One in Three;
O grant us endless length of days
In our true native land, with Thee.

name: en.literal
text: Eternal glory be to the Triune God, who giveth us life without end in our native land above.
